header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortega (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Redwood Product), Tom Li (Redwood Partner Eng), Liam O'Connor (AuroraCloud PM), Priya Narayanan (AuroraCloud Solutions Architect), Ethan Park (AuroraCloud Marketplace Eng), Sara Gomez (AuroraCloud Security)
summary: Tech sync to align on Redwood marketplace integration, reference architecture alignment, and joint solution collateral. Discussed listing requirements, auth/SSO + IAM patterns, network considerations (VPC/VPN/private deployments), packaging (container/helm/terraform), billing & support model, and pilot test plan. Action items assigned to both teams for draft listing, test account setup, and initial integration tests.
topics: Marketplace listing artifacts and acceptance criteria
Reference architecture / deployment patterns (VPC, Dedicated, Private)
Auth & IAM: SSO/SAML, role assumption, service accounts
Packaging: images, helm charts, terraform module
Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on the hour. Uh, quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, Rafael SE on the call, and Anika from product.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam here from AuroraCloud, Priya, Ethan, and Sara also on.
[00:12] Rafael Ortega: Cool, we'll keep this pretty focused, goal is to map out the marketplace listing steps and the follow-up reference-arch items.
[00:20] Priya Narayanan: Sounds good. We're trying to figure out: what does Redwood expect for marketplace packaging, and how tightly do we need to couple with your private deployment options?
[00:28] Maya Chen: Right. High-level — the marketplace listing is two parts: customer-facing listing + technical assets for deployment. For the listing we need a short description, 3 screenshots or GIFs, vendor logo, support contact, and the acceptance checklist (runbook, security attestations). For the technical side, we usually accept either a container image with helm chart and terraform module or a reference-arch with detailed deploy steps.
[00:45] Ethan Park: Quick question — do you enforce a specific registry or can we use our existing private registry?
[00:50] Rafael Ortega: We don't force a registry, but for marketplace automated installs we recommend a public or reachable registry for the installer. If you want gated installs for enterprise customers, we support private registry flows but it'll need an image pull role and docs.
[00:59] Sara Gomez: From security, we need to confirm KMS key handling and audit logs. If the integration requires customer-managed keys, what's the integration pattern?
[01:05] Anika Patel: Good question. For Private/VPC deployments the customer's KMS is used; we have an integration pattern where the deployment sets up an IAM role that can encrypt/decrypt through the customer's KMS. We'll provide sample IaC to wire that up. For hosted Redwood, we manage keys but we can support Bring-Your-Own-Key via HSM/KMS integrations for enterprise customers.
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: Okay, can you share a sample reference-arch that includes the role mappings and network diagram?
[01:27] Rafael Ortega: Yep, we'll share a reference arch. It includes three patterns: Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved pool in your account), and Private (full on-prem/VPC package). Each pattern has network diagrams, IAM snippets, and recommended security controls.
[01:38] Priya Narayanan: For the Dedicated case, we need to know how billing works — is it metered through Redwood or do we bill via marketplace invoicing?
[01:44] Maya Chen: Marketplace listing can support both. Typically, revenue/billing goes through the marketplace if you use their billing, but for Dedicated/reserved capacity we often set up a direct contract and then associate it with the marketplace listing as a reference. We'll sync with the GTM team but for the listing spec, include your preferred billing flow and our team will map it.
[01:58] Ethan Park: On auth flows, our marketplace requires SAML SSO for provisioning, plus the ability to exchange tokens for API access. How does Redwood recommend implementing token exchange?
[02:06] Rafael Ortega: We support OIDC and SAML. For token exchange we recommend using an STS pattern — customers assume a limited IAM role that Redwood uses for initial provisioning, then we hand over long-lived tokens stored in the customer's vault or use short-lived refresh tokens. We'll share an example TF snippet.
[02:20] Sara Gomez: Make sure to include rotation guidance and audit hooks — we need to show auditors where logs are sent.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Our template includes CloudTrail-style audit examples and a sample Splunk/Elastic ingest for logs.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: Great. On packaging — you mentioned Helm + Terraform. Do you accept an operator?
[02:35] Rafael Ortega: We do accept an operator if that's your preference, but it needs to be optional. For marketplace installs we prefer a declarative helm chart + terraform module that can be used in CI/CD. Operators tend to be heavier weight and some customers don't want them running in their cluster.
[02:48] Priya Narayanan: For Private deployments, how are model artifacts stored? Do they pull from Redwood or do we host models in our registry?
[02:54] Anika Patel: For Private and Dedicated, you can either pull model artifacts from Redwood's model registry (we support signed artifact pulls) or host them in your registry. We recommend signed artifacts and checksums, and for very regulated customers we support entirely on-prem model bundles delivered via secure transfer.
[03:12] Ethan Park: A bit of a picky one — our marketplace metadata needs a 500-char description and 1–2 minute demo video. Can you provide a short demo clip?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Yes, we can create a 90s demo highlighting low-latency generation and the integration flow. We'll make a short script — Rafael will demo a cold-start and warm-up with KV cache.
[03:27] Rafael Ortega: Uh, yeah, I'll capture a short run showing provisioning, token exchange, and a sample latency run. Expect artifacts in the draft listing pack.
[03:35] Liam O'Connor: On the reference-arch, we have a specific requirement: cross-account VPC access via VPC peering or Transit Gateway; some customers require private connectivity, so we need clear docs for both peering and TGW set-ups.
[03:47] Rafael Ortega: We'll include both patterns. For peering we'll show security groups and route tables; for TGW we'll show attachment steps. We'll also include notes about bandwidth and throughput for the inference traffic.
[03:56] Sara Gomez: Can you talk briefly about data residency? Some of our customers in EU require data to stay in-region.
[04:02] Anika Patel: Redwood can pin deployments to regions (and to Dedicated nodes in a specific region). For hosted inference, we can create region-specific endpoints. For Private on-prem we obviously stay local. We'll add notes to the listing about region pinning and recommended configs.
[04:16] Priya Narayanan: One operational question — if a customer wants to run an on-prem pilot, what's the minimum infra footprint? GPUs needed? 
[04:23] Rafael Ortega: For a reasonable dev pilot we recommend at least one A10/NVIDIA T4 equivalent for small throughput; for production latency-sensitive workloads you'd want multiple A100s or H100s depending on model. We'll add a sizing table in the reference arch doc. There's also a quantized CPU-friendly path but it's slower.
[04:41] Ethan Park: For the acceptance checklist, what are the required automated tests? We have a CI policy that requires smoke tests.
[04:47] Maya Chen: The marketplace acceptance typically wants: deployment smoke test (helm install), API smoke test (simple generate), auth test (SAML/OIDC role assumption), and security scan (image CVE scan). Optional: performance benchmark for a small sample prompt set. We'll share a checklist YAML.
[05:03] Liam O'Connor: Great. Regarding support, how do we handle joint incidents? Do we have a shared runbook?
[05:09] Anika Patel: We recommend a joint runbook: first-line support is the partner (AuroraCloud) for marketplace installs, Redwood handles inference/runtime issues. We'll include escalation contacts and an SLO matrix in the joint solution doc.
[05:21] Priya Narayanan: Any constraints around KV cache/continuous batching that we should highlight to customers?
[05:27] Rafael Ortega: Yes — if you rely on prefix caching across requests, we recommend sticky routing or session affinity. Batching introduces latency tradeoffs; we'll put recommended batch size defaults per model family in the doc.
[05:38] Ethan Park: For the marketplace listing fields, is there a tech-approval step? Some partners complain about long approval cycles.
[05:44] Maya Chen: There's a tech review by the marketplace team and a security review. Typical cycle is 1–2 weeks after draft submission, assuming nothing major. If there are security concerns it can take longer. We'll try to coordinate closely to speed it up.
[05:57] Liam O'Connor: Okay, let's talk timeline. We want a soft launch in early June, pilot customers in May. Is that realistic?
[06:04] Rafael Ortega: If we get the draft listing and test account by 4/20 and run tests the following week, we can hit a May pilot for a small set. Marketplace approval for early June is plausible.
[06:14] Priya Narayanan: Sounds doable. 
[06:16] Maya Chen: Cool. I'm going to summarize next steps now.
[06:19] Maya Chen: Action items — Redwood will share draft listing & assets by 4/16; AuroraCloud to send test account and IAM details by 4/20; Rafael will run the smoke tests and share results by 4/26; we schedule joint reference-arch review 4/22.
[06:35] Ethan Park: Quick clarifying question — for the TF snippets, do you prefer modules or inline examples?
[06:40] Rafael Ortega: Modules please; makes reuse easier for repo and for our customers. We'll include an example module and a minimal inline example for quickstart.
[06:48] Sara Gomez: From a security checklist perspective, can you provide the minimum permissions required (least privilege)?
[06:52] Anika Patel: Yes, the IAM snippet includes least-privilege roles and a readme explaining required perms. We'll add that to the draft.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: Any thoughts on joint marketing collateral? We want a joint solution brief and a reference-arch whitepaper.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood marketing can create a co-branded brief once the joint solution doc is in draft. We'll put that on the next steps.
[07:12] Priya Narayanan: Perfect. Thanks all.
[07:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the draft assets and schedule.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, bye.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
